hot.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
hot.summary: The survey organizes mechanistic interpretability (MI) methods and proposes five dimensions for evaluating their claims. It distinguishes output testing and detectable signals from causal explanations and reliable control. In a trained sleeper-agent backdoor setting, a linear probe detected triggered behavior with over 99% AUROC; this does not show that MI makes systems safer or generalizes beyond that trigger.

hot.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
hot.summary: VFlash generates spatial plans for vision-language models by drafting complete structured primitives, such as trajectories, in parallel, while retaining target-verified decoding for text. On MolmoSpaces, a world action model using VFlash plans reaches 70.2% success versus 61.0% with autoregressive plans. On Jetson Thor, batch-one model-pipeline latency is 703.3 ms versus 3,552.7 ms; this is not full robot response time.

hot.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
hot.summary: Scientist World turns empirical AI research papers into runnable environments where agents reproduce methods, set improvement targets, package tasks, and verify them. Its release contains 1,000 environments, while tests cover ten lower-compute environments. Attempts improved over reproduced methods in 84% of Improve runs and 74% of Innovate runs, measured by held-out gains; Innovate has more regressions.

hot.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small
hot.summary: Inkling 2 Small is Thinking Machines Lab's second model generation: a 594B-total, 17B-active Mixture-of-Experts model with a 292M-parameter vision encoder and variable effort. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, launching on Tinker with closed weights ahead of a planned Apache 2.0 weight release after external safety testing. The post covers its coding, autoresearch, vision, knowledge work and alignment results alongside details of its pretraining and a single joint RL run.

hot.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
hot.summary: SLA teaches a vision-language-action policy spatial structure by aligning its intermediate visual features with a frozen 3D perception model during continual pre-training and task-specific post-training, without adding depth as a policy input. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, both-stage alignment reaches 72.3% success, above either single-stage alternative; this result supports the combined recipe in the tested setup, not universal causation.

hot.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
hot.summary: TKCC enables agents to optimize inference deployments as workloads change by hot-reloading candidate forward passes in a persistent engine, screening them before representative measurements. Its cost model selects GPU-parallelism configurations. On B200 GLM 5.3, two-tier measurement evaluated 1,354 candidates versus 168 for a single slow tier and found a 7.2% faster solution; the result is specific to that comparison.

hot.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
hot.summary: SwarmEvolve uses many agents to search for scientific and mathematical programs, sharing internal model memories instead of lengthy text. A synthesizer writes candidate programs, which an evaluator scores. Across 21 problems, Qwen3 8B averaged 0.804, versus CodeEvolve’s 0.700, in 60-minute runs. Its median time to reach OpenEvolve’s 60-minute score was 7 minutes, a time-to-target result, not a universal win.

hot.title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels
hot.summary: MAC-v2 uses latent prediction and action chunks for offline visual reinforcement learning, training its representation for prediction and behavior cloning. It selects candidate chunks from a behavior-cloning policy using a learned Q-value. On OGBench’s visual puzzle-3x3 family, it averages 95 ± 4% success, versus 22 ± 1% for FQL. These simulated results do not establish real-world deployment.

hot.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: On-policy distillation trains a language-model student on its own continuations using a teacher’s token-level feedback. The authors trace how feedback changes parameters and predictions, and how those changes redirect training prefixes. A larger teacher transfers less than a smaller RL-trained sibling: the same 1.5B student reaches AIME accuracy of 0.31 versus 0.45. Findings are limited to models and settings tested.

hot.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
hot.summary: Social Humanoid enables a humanoid robot to generate and execute responses to human movement during close-range interactions. It retargets human-human motion captures into interaction-aware human-robot examples and maps human and robot motion into a shared vocabulary. On a Unitree G1, high-five trials reached 90% real-world success; this measures task completion and safe tracking, not social appropriateness.

hot.title: You don't need long context
hot.summary: The authors test whether agents need full histories or documents in active context using compact handoff states and tool-based retrieval. In long-horizon and long-input tasks these approaches preserve or improve results. For Qwen 3 Coder Next, a 16K rather than 256K context window yielded 7× more decoded tokens per second; this measures throughput, not task time, and evidence is limited.

hot.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
hot.summary: The authors describe a recurring process for auditing and repairing agent benchmark tasks using reports and traces, agent-proposed diagnoses, reference-solution checks, and human review. In Terminal-Bench 2.0, they revised 28 of 89 tasks. Across 19 agents, scores changed by up to 12 percentage points, while rankings remained highly correlated (Spearman rho = 0.958); close rankings could still shift.

hot.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
hot.summary: Interactive Visual Gym evaluates visual assistants in simulated tasks where user actions and task state can change in response to advice. Its benchmark covers cooking, household, and mobile-interface tasks. Under measured response latency, Gemini 4 Argon’s CookSim in-time success falls from 60.9% to 33.1%, showing a timing effect in simulated rollouts, not a real-world forecast.

hot.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
hot.summary: SplatAnything uses feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct scenes from images without per-scene optimization. It introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which scales geometry using median neighboring-point spacing rather than mean camera distance. In a four-view ablation, GSNorm scores 0.198/0.245 DISTS/LPIPS, below RDNorm and scale calibration. On pose-free Mip-NeRF 360, LPIPS is 0.463 versus Mirror2-GS’s 0.528, within benchmark settings.

hot.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: The authors introduce targeted guidance for multi-turn software-engineering reinforcement learning, placing textual feedback before a failing turn and distilling the same model’s hint-conditioned token predictions only there, alongside ordinary rewards. In their coding setup, Markdown reward is 0.85 ± 0.09 versus 0.00 ± 0.00 for GRPO, while coding pass-rate is 0.33 ± 0.05 versus 0.33 ± 0.07; findings are limited to this setting and designed feedback.

hot.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
hot.summary: RoboARCade benchmarks agentic robot control across 22 simulated tasks with varied starting conditions. In this setting, agents observe scenes and choose controller targets directly in a closed loop. Results show strategy and precise execution are larger failure sources than visual understanding, while success claims are often incorrect. On a five-task subset, experience raises mean rubric score from 53.5% to 73%.

hot.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
hot.summary: FrontierPhysics evaluates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended physics research from high-level briefs. The benchmark uses physicist-contributed research tasks and grades structured outputs with deterministic checks, alongside manuscripts and research trajectories against expert-authored rubrics. Passing requires all verifier tests and blocking criteria. The top tested configuration passed 46/168 trials (27.4%), measuring performance under this protocol rather than human publication acceptance.

hot.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
hot.summary: EgoGeneralist uses a pretrained video model to generate first-person video conditioned on rendered metric action and recover metric action from Posegrid latents. It renders action as an ego-view map for video control and a multiview Posegrid for action readout. On 99 HOT3D target-reaching tasks, it records 3.81 cm mean minimum distance versus VITRA’s 6.32 cm, without establishing real-world robot execution.

hot.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
hot.summary: The authors compare disclosure policies in controlled economic games, holding markets, models, incentives, and interaction rules fixed. They measure proposed opportunities and final outcomes. Full disclosure lowers GPT-6 Sol's trade gains from 97.7% to 90.8%, but raises Claude Sonnet 5's from 72.1% to 85.6%. Results vary by model and setting; deployed systems remain untested.

hot.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone
hot.summary: BabyTheorist tests whether learners acquire reusable rules from ungrouped visual examples and apply them to new cases. It trains on unlabeled before-and-after grids generated by hidden programs, then evaluates transfer across a curriculum. Seven representative baselines stop within the first two of eight levels; NEO reaches Level 2 in Single modes but fails Level 1 in Multi modes.

likes.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
likes.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.

likes.title: Mistral Large 4
likes.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model whose authors examine long-context attention for agentic coding. They find architecture variants with similar language-modeling loss can differ on SWE-bench Verified, while knowledge-based evaluations show no analogous gap. The final system restores long-context access in more layers and uses DSA to select past tokens; its benchmark results do not isolate DSA’s effect.

likes.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² teaches an evolver reusable guidance for changing a frozen model’s task harness during a run, rather than selecting one harness for every task. Its Meta-Skill guides when to edit, hold, or avoid changes; edits remain run-local, without held-out verifier feedback. With GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports mean@5 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and mean@3 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1, on two tested benchmarks.

likes.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
likes.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

likes.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
likes.summary: The authors test whether on-policy distillation transfers specialist improvements beyond supervised tasks. A student learns from its own responses with teacher guidance; multi-teacher training routes domains to matching teachers. Narrow math supervision nearly matches teacher scores in-distribution but leaves out-of-distribution performance 3.73% below base. Broader data with a stronger teacher raises scores across five benchmarks, but effects are not isolated.

likes.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
likes.summary: The authors use speculative decoding to steer selected decisions into less noisy context positions. A trained draft is more likely to be rejected at those points, so the target resamples at the start of a fresh verification block while preserving its token distribution. On DeepSWE, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 pass rate rises from 60.6% to 67.6%; not all benchmark gains are statistically established.

likes.title: Automating AI R&D for Molecular Discovery
likes.summary: Intology evaluates Locus, its autonomous AI R&D system, on three molecular discovery tasks: proprietary molecular property prediction, adapting Boltz-2 for small-molecule potency prediction, and designing antibody workflows around BoltzGen/Boltz-2 and ESMC/ESMFold2. Under matched compute, Locus outperforms Claude Code, Codex, and baselines from Boltz and BioHub, generalizing better from limited data and finding more sample-efficient solutions.

likes.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
likes.summary: IdeaTaste tests whether AI research agents make choices resembling those of human communities. It generates proposals from literature frozen at the end of 2025, then compares their citations and ideas with papers published in January–August 2026. Agents reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, but publication similarity measures community choices, not objective research quality.

likes.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
likes.summary: GSBR guides online robot learning by penalizing actions only outside neighborhoods around sampled actions from a pretrained controller. This lets the actor choose among supported behaviors while permitting nearby improvements at a distance-based cost. Across 19 tasks in four benchmarks, GSBR averages 95% success and 0.95 normalized throughput, versus RLT’s 0.77; on LIBERO, RLT has higher success.

likes.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-Filled 3-Manifolds Along Fundamental Shadow Link Complements With Big Volume
likes.summary: The authors prove large-level asymptotics for Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants of hyperbolic 3-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn filling fundamental shadow link complements. They extend quantum 6j symbols and use approximate reflection symmetry to cancel problematic Fourier coefficients while preserving asymptotics. Both conjectures hold at positive odd levels when manifold volume is sufficiently close to the starting complement’s; this does not cover all fillings.

likes.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
likes.summary: CoworkOS addresses complex work by letting a Main Agent direct delegated tasks while a Coordinator tracks assignments and feedback, and Subagents execute bounded work. Persistent jobs, memory, and shared resources support continuity across interruptions. In a five-round post-training case study, the mean across eight benchmark scores rose from 33.19 to 42.95; this measured increase does not isolate CoworkOS’s causal effect.

likes.title: Introducing Ripple-65B Preview, a Frontier Open-Weight Model
likes.summary: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary language model that powers its AI chip design platform. The dense 65B model was trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context, and reaches 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a new U.S. open-weight state of the art for agentic coding. The full R&D cost was $32M, which the team estimates is one-tenth that of the previous open-weight SOTA.

likes.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
likes.summary: DreamX transfers motion from human videos to robot actions without paired human–robot training data. It uses learnable queries to read a pretrained video model’s features and compress motion into a code, which can condition future-video generation or robot action prediction. On LARYBench, it achieves 0.17 average normalized action MSE and 69.67% accuracy; transfer is demonstrated only in evaluated open-loop settings.
